judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Key Unit Competences at the same canonical Grade coordinate (P3, rank 2) under the merged 'TOPIC AREA: GEOMETRY' parent, but in distinct Units with distinct substance. The first (Unit 10, Types of lines and angles) targets identifying and drawing parallel, perpendicular and intersecting lines and drawing/comparing right, acute and obtuse angles; the second (Unit 11, Square, rectangle, triangle and circle) targets drawing and describing those figures and finding perimeter. The line- and angle-level skills (notably perpendicularity/right angles and parallel lines, plus drawing accuracy) are constituent competencies of accurately drawing and describing squares, rectangles and triangles, so proficiency in the first substantively supports success in the second; the second additionally extends to closed figures and perimeter measurement, a broadening beyond generic repetition. Shared Topic Area, Grade, and the 'pupils will be able to draw' wording overlap were treated as nomination signals only. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence, so the judgment rests on the complete, non-truncated competence statements supplied.
